commands.review_summary:
The PR adds a 120-second default timeout for memory remote HTTP requests without an abort signal and forwards explicit timeout overrides through `postJson`.

PR surface: Source +15, Tests +110. Total +125 across 4 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main has an unbounded unsignaled response-acquisition path, and the proposed branch clearly retains an unbounded path when a supplied signal never aborts. I did not execute the contributor branch during this read-only review.

target.title: fix(memory): bound unsignaled remote HTTP with default timeoutMs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory remote HTTP (`withRemoteHttpResponse`) only forwarded an optional caller `AbortSignal`. Embedding batch / `postJson` callers often omit a signal (Google/OpenAI/Voyage upload and status polls), so a peer that accepts TCP but never returns headers could hang the Gateway forever. Idle body caps never start until headers arrive.

## Why This Change Was Made

When callers omit `signal`, install a shared hang floor via existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs`:

- Default: `MEMORY_REMOTE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` = 120s (aligned with memory remote batch budgets so large uploads are not clamped below established policy)
- Explicit `timeoutMs` override still wins
- Callers that already pass `AbortSignal` keep their own deadline (no default floor)

Also forward optional `timeoutMs` through `postJson` so production JSON POST callers can override the floor without reimplementing the wrapper.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** Unsignaled memory remote HTTP (embedding batch upload/status, shared `postJson`) could hang indefinitely on a stalled upstream.

**After:** Unsignaled requests fail closed after 120s (`TimeoutError` / `request timed out`). Callers with `AbortSignal` keep their budget.

## Evidence

- Changed: `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/remote-http.ts`, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/post-json.ts`
- Production path under test: `withRemoteHttpResponse` (shared by `postJson` / batch-upload / provider embedding batches) against a real local `node:http` server that never writes headers
- Regression: `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/remote-http.test.ts`, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/post-json.test.ts`

### Caller-path hang proof (Vitest)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/remote-http.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/post-json.test.ts --reporter=verbose

## Real behavior proof

**Commands run:**
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/remote-http.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/post-json.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**Before fix:**
Unsignaled `withRemoteHttpResponse` / `postJson` forwarded no `timeoutMs` to `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, so a peer that accepted TCP and never returned headers could hang until process restart.

**After fix:**
With a short `timeoutMs` override (stand-in for the 120s production floor), hung POST/GET requests reject with `TimeoutError: request timed out`. Mocked calls assert the default floor is `MEMORY_REMOTE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` when `signal` is omitted, and that caller signals suppress the default floor.
